Fit a characteristic function that is a linear mix of independent sources

Source: R/from_cf_structured.R
from_cf_sources.Rd

Fits a distribution of the form \(X = A S + G\), where the coordinates of \(S\) are independent and not Gaussian, \(A\) is an invertible matrix and \(G\) is Gaussian noise or absent. Only the characteristic function of \(X\) is needed. The mixing matrix is read from cf, and each source is then fitted in one dimension with from_cf(). A joint fit in n_dim dimensions would be less accurate.

Usage

from_cf_sources(
  cf,
  n_dim,
  N,
  n_freq = 8192L,
  bandwidths = c(0.3, 0.6, 1.2, 2.5, 5),
  max_iter = 300L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

cf, n_dim

As in from_cf(). n_dim must be at least 2.

N

Number of mixture components for each source.

n_freq, bandwidths, max_iter

Passed to from_cf() for each source.

seed

Optional integer seed. When supplied, the random number generator state is restored on exit.

Value

A list of class proxymix_cf_sources with

  • mixing, the matrix \(\hat A\). Its columns are the mixing directions, scaled so that each coordinate of \(Z = \hat A^{-1} X\) has unit variance. Column order and sign are not identified.

  • sources, a list of n_dim one-dimensional gmm_fit objects, the fits to the coordinates of \(Z\).

  • noise_cov, the off-diagonal covariance of \(Z\), with the diagonal set to zero. It is zero when there is no noise. The noise variance on the diagonal stays inside sources.

  • cf(t), the characteristic function of the fit at the rows of t.

  • draw(n), an n by n_dim matrix of draws from the fit.

  • project(direction, max_components = 1e5), the gmm of \(a^\top X\) under the fit for a direction \(a\). Sources whose coefficient is below 1e-3 of the largest are replaced by a single normal with the same mean and variance. It gives an error if the projection needs more than max_components components.

  • diagnostics, with off_diagonal (the largest off-diagonal entry divided by the largest diagonal entry of the Hessian difference at the third frequency, transformed by the inverse of mixing, 0 if the sources are separated exactly, with a warning above 0.05), dependence (the largest over pairs of coordinates of \(Z\) of the root of the integral, against the standard normal density in two dimensions, of the squared modulus of the joint characteristic function minus the product of the marginal ones, with the Gaussian noise term allowed for; 0 for independent sources, with a warning above 0.01), imaginary (the largest imaginary part of the directions before it is dropped) and heldout_rms (the root mean square of the difference between cf and the fit's characteristic function on fresh frequencies).

Details

The fitted family, independent sources that are each a one-dimensional Gaussian mixture, is the independent factor model of Attias (1999), who fits it to a sample by maximum likelihood.

The result is a list, not a gmm. As a single mixture it would need N^n_dim components. It has three functions: cf(), draw() (sampling from the fit) and project() (the one-dimensional mixture along a direction). draw() gives an error when the noise covariance estimated from cf is too far from positive semi-definite to be sampled.

The mixing matrix is found from second derivatives of the logarithm of cf at two random frequencies (Yeredor, 2000). The coordinates it separates are then tested for pairwise independence with the criterion of Eriksson and Koivunen (2003), which compares the joint characteristic function of each pair with the product of the two marginal ones at all frequencies. If the criterion is above 0.01 the frequencies are drawn again, up to four times, and the directions with the smallest value are kept.

The target must have a finite, positive definite covariance. A warning of class proxymix_cf_not_sources is raised when the criterion is still above 0.01, or when the directions do not separate the sources at a third frequency. Either is the sign that the target is not of the form above.

References

Attias, H. (1999). Independent factor analysis. Neural Computation, 11(4), 803–851. doi:10.1162/089976699300016458

Eriksson, J., and Koivunen, V. (2003). Characteristic-function-based independent component analysis. Signal Processing, 83(10), 2195–2208. doi:10.1016/S0165-1684(03)00162-2

Yeredor, A. (2000). Blind source separation via the second characteristic function. Signal Processing, 80(5), 897–902. doi:10.1016/S0165-1684(00)00062-1

See also

from_cf(), from_cf_elliptical().

Other fitting: fit_em_samples(), fit_kld_em(), fit_moment_match(), fit_mppca_samples(), from_cf(), from_cf_elliptical(), from_kde(), from_objective(), select_N()

Examples

## Two independent Gamma(3) sources, mixed, with N(0, 0.25 I) noise.
A <- matrix(c(0.7, 0.3, 0, -0.7), 2L)
cf <- function(t) {
  u <- t %*% A
  (1 - 1i * u[, 1])^(-3) * (1 - 1i * u[, 2])^(-3) *
    exp(-0.125 * rowSums(t^2))
}
fit <- from_cf_sources(cf, n_dim = 2L, N = 3L, n_freq = 1024L, seed = 1L)
fit$diagnostics$off_diagonal
#> [1] 2.906809e-06
first <- fit$project(c(1, 0))
gmm_cf_distance(first, function(s) cf(cbind(s[, 1], 0)))$distance
#> [1] 0.002356499
